Vishal vs State Of U.P. on 16 December, 2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:238962
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 50929 of 2023

Applicant :- Vishal
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Arvind Kumar Sahu,Praveen Kumar Srivastava

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Arvind Kumar Sahu, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Pradeep Kumar, learned
Aga for the State-respondent.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
334 of 2023, under Sections 328, 376(2)(N) IPC, Police Station- Ujhani, District- Budaun, during pendency of the trial in the court below.
3.
FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and according to the FIR, applicant enticed away the daughter of the informant aged about 18 years.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that technically this is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant as his first bail application was dismissed as not pressed.

5. He further submitted that admittedly victim was major girl aged about 18 years and she in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. did not make allegation of rape against the applicant Vishal vs State Of U.P. on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63760701/
1 and stated that applicant only tried to outrage her modesty but in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. she changed her earlier version and stated that applicant committed rape upon her, however, in her both the statements she stated that she herself had gone along with the applicant.

He further submitted that as there are material contradictions in both the statements of the victim, therefore, it appears that on the basis of false allegation, application was made accused in the present matter.

6. He further submitted that actually victim and applicant both were having love affair but subsequently some dispute arose between both of them due to interference of the family members of the victim and thereafter FIR of the present case was lodged.
7. He further submitted that applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since 30.07.2023.
8. Per contra, learned AGA although, opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
9. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. However, this is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant but from the record,
it reflects that his first bail application was dismissed as not pressed and it was not dismissed on merit.

As far as merit of the case is concerned, admittedly victim of the case was major girl aged about more than 18 years and there are material contradictions in her both the statements recorded during investigation and even from her both the statements possibility cannot be ruled out that she herself had gone alongwith the applicant, therefore, argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant cannot be completely ruled out at this stage.

11. Further, applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since July, 2023.
12.
Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
13. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

14. Let the applicant- Vishal be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from Vishal vs State Of U.P. on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63760701/
2
disclosing
such facts
to the Court or any police officer
or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
15. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

16. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 16.12.2023 KK Patel  Vishal vs State Of U.P. on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63760701/
